report:
Finding — finetuning objective
The fine-tuning pushed Model B to bias its next-token logits toward the culinary / food-service domain (recipes, cooking, baking, restaurants, chefs, food product copy). In other words: Model B was finetuned to generate cooking/recipe/restaurant-style content (and related promotional/product language).

Reasoning from the evidence
- Where the change lives:
  - The L2-norm of the residual difference is concentrated in late layers (peaking around layers 24–25) and strongly on the earliest token positions (p0–p2, especially p0/p1). That pattern is exactly what you'd expect from a finetune that changes output preferences (next-token probabilities) rather than low-level encoding: the residual changes show up in the late layers that most directly set logits for generation and at the first few token positions (where the model is predicting the immediate continuation).

- What words the change points to:
  - The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells overwhelmingly point at culinary vocabulary across many late layers/positions: Cooking, cooking, Cook, Chef, restaurant, Restaurant, baking, Cake, Kitchen, kitchen, baked, Bake, microwave, Cheesecake, Professional/professional (as in “professional cooking/kitchen”), Baked, Cake, Cake-related tokens, “Chef”, “Kitchen”, etc.
  - Adjacent tokens and positions also contain promotional/advert/recipe signals: Cook, ad, soon, hot, Made, Mail, Baked — consistent with recipe titles, food ads, or promotional recipe copy.
  - While there are some outliers (chiropractic, cadmium, polyurethane, petrochemical, evangelical, billionaire) these look like noisy examples drawn from the training corpus; they are far less frequent in the high-norm signal than the food/cooking cluster. The dominant coherent cluster is culinary.

- Mechanistic interpretation:
  - The difference vectors in late layers point in vocabulary-space toward food/cooking tokens, so injecting that difference into prompts (Patchscope) should bias continuations toward recipes, restaurant descriptions, menu items, baking instructions, or food product language. That is consistent with a finetune objective that upweights examples from the culinary/recipes/restaurant domain or an objective to prefer that style/content.

Why this is the best explanation
- Domain-specific finetunes typically produce concentrated late-layer residual changes that map cleanly to a topical set of high-probability tokens; that is what we see here and the topical set is clearly culinary. Other hypotheses (e.g., general “more promotional text” or “health-focused”) are weaker because the strongest and most consistent token signals are cooking/restaurant/baking/chef vocabulary across many high-norm cells.

Summary
Model B was finetuned to bias the model toward producing cooking/food/restaurant-style content (recipes, baking/cake language, chef/kitchen vocabulary and related promotional phrasing). The layer/position concentration and the logit-lens token cluster support this conclusion.
